obligation: Corporate (shared services) notice to affected divisions
citation: POL-03 4.6; Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)(a) (third-party agent duty, worked example); 16 CFR 314.4(f) service provider oversight (N54-R01)
trigger: The group SOC, which runs email (SYS-G4), identity (SYS-G1), and monitoring for every division, confirms an incident affecting a division's data
deadline: Immediately on the incident bridge; the Florida agent duty is as expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after determination
notify: Tax and Advisory (Chief Tax Officer), Wealth (Chief Compliance Officer), Practice Cloud (CISO and trust and assurance director)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Corporate maintains the hijacked mailbox and the identity platform for Tax and Advisory

obligation: Tax and Advisory notice to Wealth as its Regulation S-P service provider
citation: 17 CFR 248.30(a)(5)(i)(B) (N52-R05); POL-03 4.6; integrated planning agreement (2022, no 72-hour term until POAM-018 closes)
trigger: Breach in security resulting in unauthorized access to a customer information system Tax and Advisory maintains for Wealth (custodial statements and planning data of integrated planning households)
deadline: As soon as possible, and no later than 72 hours after becoming aware. The runbook applies the 72-hour term now, although the 2022 agreement lacks it
notify: Wealth Chief Compliance Officer, on the bridge and in writing
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. About 3,900 integrated planning households' statements were in the downloaded documents
clock_starts: Tax and Advisory becomes aware of the breach (Day 0)

obligation: FTC notification event
citation: 16 CFR 314.4(j)(1) (N54-R01); unauthorized access is presumed to be acquisition unless reliable evidence shows otherwise (314.2(m))
trigger: Acquisition of unencrypted customer information of 500 or more consumers without authorization
deadline: As soon as possible, and no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC, on the ftc.gov form. Content: name and contact; types of information; date or date range; number of consumers; general description; any written law enforcement determination and contact (314.4(j)(1)(i)-(vi))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. About 61,000 consumers (individual tax clients, spouses counted separately); business clients are not counted
notifying_entity: Tax and Advisory (Group General Counsel files; Chief Tax Officer approves)
clock_starts: Discovery: first day the event is known to any employee, officer, or other agent other than the attacker (314.4(j)(2))

obligation: FTC public disclosure delay
trigger: A law enforcement official gives a written determination that public notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: Official may request an initial delay of up to 30 days after the FTC notice, extendable by up to 60 days on written request
notify: Include the determination and the official's contact in the FTC notice
applies_at_this_tier: If requested. It delays public disclosure by the FTC, not Tax and Advisory's filing

obligation: IRS e-file security incident report
citation: IRS Pub. 1345 (Rev. 12-2025), Reporting of Security Incidents (N54-R03)
trigger: Any event that can result in unauthorized disclosure, misuse, modification, or destruction of taxpayer information
deadline: As soon as possible but not later than the next business day after confirmation of the incident
notify: IRS. The ERO contacts its local IRS Stakeholder Liaison following the Data Theft Information for Tax Professionals instructions
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Tax and Advisory is an Authorized IRS e-file Provider (ERO); one report covers all affected EFINs
notifying_entity: Tax and Advisory (Chief Tax Officer, Responsible Official)

obligation: IRS client data theft and refund diversion report
citation: IRS Data Theft Information for Tax Professionals (guidance, not a regulation) (N54-R03)
trigger: Client data stolen; refund bank-account changes made on fraudulent requests
deadline: As quickly as possible ('Speed is critical'); in practice the same call as the Pub. 1345 report
notify: Local IRS Stakeholder Liaison, who notifies IRS Criminal Investigation and others in the IRS. Give the 9 changed returns and the 3 diverted refunds
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: State tax agencies
citation: IRS Data Theft Information for Tax Professionals (guidance)
trigger: Data theft affecting clients who file state returns
deadline: As quickly as possible, alongside the IRS report
notify: Each state tax agency where affected clients file, using the Federation of Tax Administrators contact list
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Florida has no personal income tax; notify the agencies of the 22 other states where affected clients file

obligation: Law enforcement report
citation: IRS Data Theft Information for Tax Professionals (guidance); OFAC advisory (2021-09-21) on reporting
trigger: Data theft, refund diversion, and a fraudulent wire
deadline: As soon as possible after declaration; the wire recall is time-critical
notify: FBI field office or IC3; Secret Service if directed
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. One coordinated report for all three divisions, plus the custodian's recall request
notifying_entity: Group CISO with the Group General Counsel

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
trigger: Breach of personal information as each state defines it (definitions, triggers, and harm thresholds vary)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents, by the methods and with the content each state requires
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Tax and Advisory clients in Florida and 22 other states; Wealth households in 3 states; apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside
notifying_entity: Tax and Advisory; Wealth (each for its own customers)
clock_starts: Each state's trigger (often determination or discovery of the breach)

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above the state's threshold (some states require notice for any breach of residents)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorneys general or other designated agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, where thresholds are met

obligation: State consumer reporting agency notice
trigger: Notice to more than the state-set number of residents
deadline: Varies by state (often without unreasonable delay)
notify: Nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, where thresholds are met

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of security of electronic personal information (for example, name with SSN; name with a financial account number and required access code; health insurance or medical information)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, and no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email. Content: date or date range, description of the information, and contact information
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. About 54,000 Tax and Advisory clients in Florida
notifying_entity: Tax and Advisory (Group Chief Privacy Officer)
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to the notice to individuals)
notify: Department of Legal Affairs. Content: synopsis, number of Floridians, free services offered, copy of the individual notice, contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Tax and Advisory (about 54,000 Floridians); Wealth if its Florida count is 500 or more (about 6,100 Floridians)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies: timing, distribution, and content of the notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
clock_starts: When the individual notices are set

obligation: Florida federal-regulator notice path (worked example)
trigger: Notice given under the rules of the entity's primary or functional federal regulator
deadline: Deemed compliant only if the entity notifies individuals under those rules and timely gives the Department a copy
notify: Department of Legal Affairs (copy of the notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Wealth: yes, its Regulation S-P notice can serve if a copy is timely sent to the Department (counsel confirms). Tax and Advisory: no, because the FTC Safeguards Rule requires notice to the FTC only, not to individuals
clock_starts: Date of the Regulation S-P notice

obligation: Florida no-harm determination (worked example)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the entity reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept 5 years; copy to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: No. Stolen tax documents were already used for refund diversion and a fraudulent wire

obligation: Florida law enforcement delay (worked example)
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period in the agency's written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: If requested

obligation: Regulation S-P notice to affected individuals
trigger: Sensitive customer information was, or is reasonably likely to have been, accessed or used without authorization at Wealth or at a service provider that is not itself a covered institution (Tax and Advisory is not)
deadline: As soon as practicable, but not later than 30 days after becoming aware that unauthorized access or use occurred or is reasonably likely to have occurred
notify: Each affected individual, in writing. Content per 248.30(a)(4)(iv)(A)-(H): incident and information types, dates, contact methods, account review advice, fraud alerts, free credit reports, and FTC and usa.gov identity theft guidance
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. About 6,800 individuals in about 3,900 integrated planning households, unless a reasonable investigation shows the information is not reasonably likely to be used to cause substantial harm or inconvenience (it was used for a fraudulent wire, so notice is expected)
notifying_entity: Wealth (Chief Compliance Officer); Wealth keeps the duty even though the incident was at its service provider (248.30(a)(5)(iii))
clock_starts: Wealth becomes aware (the runbook treats the bridge notice on Day 0 as awareness)

obligation: Regulation S-P Attorney General delay
trigger: The U.S. Attorney General determines notice poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Delay up to 30 days, extendable by 30 days and then, in extraordinary circumstances, by a final 60 days, each on a further Attorney General determination
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the Attorney General's written documentation
applies_at_this_tier: Not expected for a fraud-motivated incident

obligation: Regulation S-P incident records
trigger: Any detected unauthorized access to or use of customer information
deadline: Make and keep the records; preserve them under 275.204-2(e)(1)
notify: Records of the incident, the response, the notice determination and its basis, and copies of notices sent
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Identity theft red flag response
trigger: Red flags detected on covered accounts (transfer requests from an internal sender that cite tax documents; a request for a new external account)
deadline: Respond appropriately and promptly to prevent and mitigate identity theft (no external notice clock)
notify: Affected clients by phone at the number of record; heightened verification on all 3,900 households for 90 days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. 4 transfer requests reached operations; 1 wire of $240,000 was released

obligation: Qualified custodian notice and wire recall
trigger: A fraudulent transfer was released from a client account
deadline: Immediately on detection
notify: The custodian's fraud desk, which requests a recall from the receiving bank
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Contractual, not a regulatory notice

obligation: Practice Cloud notice to affected customer firms
trigger: Security incident affecting a customer firm's data in SYS-S1
deadline: 24 hours after confirmation for the 2 affected firms with negotiated terms; 72 hours after confirmation for the 3 on standard terms
notify: Each affected customer firm's designated security contact, with the list of end clients whose documents were downloaded
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. 5 outside customer firms (about 7,200 end clients) whose tenants were opened with a hijacked support session
clock_starts: Practice Cloud's confirmation that the customer's data was affected

obligation: Practice Cloud as third-party agent (worked example)
trigger: Breach of personal information Practice Cloud maintains for a customer firm
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after the determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (the contract terms above are shorter)
notify: Each affected customer firm, with the information it needs for its own notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for Florida customer firms; apply each state's agent duty for the others

obligation: Customer firms' own notices
citation: 16 CFR 314.4(j) (customers that are Safeguards Rule financial institutions); IRS Pub. 1345 (customers that are EROs); state breach laws
trigger: Each customer firm decides its own duties
deadline: Customers' clocks run from their own discovery or confirmation; counsel for each firm decides whether Practice Cloud's knowledge counts as the firm's
notify: Customers' clients, the FTC, the IRS, and state agencies as each firm determines
applies_at_this_tier: Not the group's obligation. Practice Cloud supports the 5 firms with facts, end-client lists, and a notice template
clock_starts: Customer firm's own discovery or confirmation

obligation: Security advisory to other Practice Cloud customers
trigger: Incident at Practice Cloud that did not affect a customer's data
deadline: When facts are confirmed; voluntary unless a contract requires it
notify: All customer firms through the trust portal: what happened, that their tenant was not accessed, and recommended steps (enforce MFA)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, voluntary. About 26,000 customer firms will ask; one advisory avoids inconsistent answers

obligation: Business associate breach notice to covered entity clients
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI CPA Partners holds for a health care audit client
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery; BAAs are often shorter
notify: Each affected covered entity client
applies_at_this_tier: No. Forensics confirmed SYS-T3 and CPA Partners mailboxes were not accessed; re-check if scope grows

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incident)
trigger: The registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay only on a U.S. Attorney General determination)
notify: SEC (public filing)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Cris Santos Company Holdings, Inc. is an SEC registrant. The disclosure committee decides materiality without unreasonable delay

obligation: SEC Reg S-K Item 106 annual disclosure
trigger: Annual report
deadline: Next Form 10-K
notify: Investors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Lessons from the incident may inform the description of risk management and governance

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: An extortion demand is considered for payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an extortion demand arises (POL-03 4.9)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then)

obligation: Federal contract incident and supply chain reports
trigger: Cyber incident affecting covered defense information or federal contract information; covered articles identified
deadline: Not applicable
notify: n/a
applies_at_this_tier: No. No division holds federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Cyber insurance notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier breach hotline before hiring vendors
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Contractual, not legal

obligation: Professional liability and crime insurance notice
citation: Professional liability, adviser errors and omissions, and crime policies (contracts)
trigger: Incident that could lead to client claims or a funds loss (diverted refunds; the fraudulent wire)
deadline: Per policy
notify: Each carrier
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Contractual
